title: Release notes on the first start after an upgrade (/whats-new)
behavior: After upgrading the package, the first interactive pi start shows what changed since the version you last ran, once; later starts stay silent, and /whats-new shows those notes again on demand.
hint: Start pi twice in a row: the first start shows "pi-toolkits updated X → Y", the second does not. `/whats-new` re-shows the notes, `/whats-new all` lists every bundled release, `/whats-new off` silences the startup notice.

title: Permission parser: approval-log false positives 52 → 16
behavior: Routine read-only commands — grep with quoted regexes, literal for-loops over files, env pipelines, docker ps and curl with -w — no longer stop for an approval, while unresolved outputs, sudo and arbitrary code still do.
hint: In a session with /ask-perm on: `grep -n '\s*$' `, `for f in a b; do grep -n x "$f"; done`, `env | grep PI_`, `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost/` and `docker ps` should run without a dialog; `echo x > "$UNKNOWN"` and `sudo …` still ask.

title: Startup-only release notes and permission safety review fixes
behavior: An upgrade shows its release notes once on the next interactive start without adding any slash command, and shell variables or unresolved redirects that cannot be judged safely now keep asking instead of risking an allow.
hint: Start pi twice after an upgrade: the first shows the notes and the second is silent; there is no /whats-new command. With permission enabled, conditional/reassigned shell variables and unresolved redirects should still ask.
